### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f6a429b95cc183a0c1b610bf185d396c3915244a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3686ec57a8e61c9d2155a18678df5d2671a813c9` — the merge of head `2f6e606ddb7e7bb72e2257492b67a796ca61a16e` into base `f6a429b95cc183a0c1b610bf185d396c3915244a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3686ec57a8e61c9d2155a18678df5d2671a813c9 && git checkout 3686ec57a8e61c9d2155a18678df5d2671a813c9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f6a429b95cc183a0c1b610bf185d396c3915244a 2f6e606ddb7e7bb72e2257492b67a796ca61a16e && git checkout -B drift-repro f6a429b95cc183a0c1b610bf185d396c3915244a && git merge --no-ff 2f6e606ddb7e7bb72e2257492b67a796ca61a16e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f6a429b95cc183a0c1b610bf185d396c3915244a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2f6e606ddb7e7bb72e2257492b67a796ca61a16e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-bare-name-conflict.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-catalog-name-collision.test.ts + .changeset/31392-install-local-cloud-held-name-refused.md (prose face, read for ② and for agreement with the code); cited code read, not reviewed: packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`NamespaceConflictError`, `SecurityCatalogNameConflictError`, `BareNameConflictError`, `installPackage`, `registerItem`, `restoringOnRefusal`), packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts (`registerApp`, `registerPackageBody`), packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (the `manifest` service's `register`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (the `objectql` service's `manifests` getter), packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-writability.ts (`isWritablePackage`), packages/objectql/src/security-catalog-namespace.ts

Inputs: card #31392 body and its three comments (triage 6717970216, seat claim 6719651440, os-dev-report 6720254619); PR #31476 body, one commit, four-file list, `git diff origin/main...pr/31476` (merge base 1ff99441; the four paths are byte-identical between 1ff99441 and origin/main f6a429b9, so the net diff is the same against either); the head's check-runs read twice by `gh api`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Which cloud-branch installs are now refused.** The catch after `manifestService.register` (plugin.ts 3003-3037 at head) answers `422 PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED` with `Package 'id' cannot be installed: registry-sentence` when `refusesNameHeldElsewhere(err)` is true, i.e. `err.code === NAMESPACE_CONFLICT_CODE` and `err.name` is one of `NamespaceConflictError`, `SecurityCatalogNameConflictError`, `BareNameConflictError`. Read against registry.ts: all three classes carry `code = NAMESPACE_CONFLICT_CODE` and set `this.name` to exactly those strings (lines 2670, 2777, 2875). So the cloud branch now refuses: a namespace another installed non-co-owner package owns (registry.ts 8653, `collisionPolicy` not `warn`); a position, permission set or capability name held by another package, by the environment catalog or by a built-in (package door 4437 with `builtIns: true, environment: true`; item seam 7624); a bare name another package or the platform holds (4726, 4787, 7647). The return is before step 4 (`this.ledger.write`, 3067), before `syncSchemas`, before the inline seed write (3120): nothing of this door's is written, and the response carries no `data`. Holders are named by the registry's own sentence (`describeSecurityCatalogHolder`: `package "id"`, `the environment catalog (...)`, `the platform, as a built-in name no package can declare`; the namespace sentence names owner and incoming package). The three new tests pin exactly these strings.
- **Which still take the lenient restart path.** Every other throw from `manifestService.register` on the cloud branch: `hotLoadError = registerError`, warn log, ledger write, `200` with `hotLoaded: false`. The `OS_METADATA_COLLISION=warn` case throws nothing at the namespace gate (registry.ts 8645-8652) and installs as before, as the changeset says. See ④ for the refusals that still take this path and arguably should not.
- **Environment-held catalog name keeps its answer; a fresh name installs.** `SecurityCatalogNameConflictError` with `existingHolder.kind === 'environment'` is the same class and code, so the old `refusesEnvironmentHeldCatalogName` answer (422) is a subset of the new predicate's. The existing #25366 matrix (both branches × three types × fresh/upgrade/CONTROL) is unchanged in the diff and stays the CONTROL; the dev's ablation of the `SecurityCatalogNameConflictError` entry reds those six cloud-branch cases plus the bare-name file's env-held CONTROL, which is consistent with the reading. The new CONTROL (`v2-free` beside the holder, 200, `hotLoaded: true`, 2.0.0 registered and ledgered) pins that a free name installs.
- **The single predicate copies no holder rule.** `refusesNameHeldElsewhere` reads `code` and `name` only; `NAME_HELD_ELSEWHERE_REFUSALS` is a set of three class names. No `conflicts`, `existingHolder`, `kind`, catalog type or bare-name type is read anywhere in the door's diff. The removed `existingHolder.kind === 'environment'` read was the last holder reading in this door. The card's "reuse the recognisers (code + name), no copy of any holder rule" is met.
- **The inline branch's answers are unchanged.** The `if (inlineManifest)` arm (3009-3014) precedes the new `if` and is untouched: every register failure on the inline branch is still `422 PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED` with `Failed to register imported manifest: ...`. Step 1f's code is unchanged (only its comment moved from "a separate decision" to "the registry's namespace gate's, 422 at the register below"); the `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` for a writable-base holder still answers first on both branches.
- **A ledger entry an earlier build wrote this way, at boot.** `rehydrate` (1698-1803) reads every entry, calls `manifestService.register` inside a per-entry try/catch, and on a throw logs `rehydrate failed for id` at error and continues. The namespace gate, the security-catalog door and (after the cold-boot seal) the bare-name door run again at every `installPackage`, so such an entry is refused at every boot, is not loaded, stays in the ledger, and is listed by GET as installed with no `notLoaded` marker (`refusedAtRehydrate` records protocol incompatibility only). "Read as before" in the changeset and PR body is accurate as a statement of no behaviour change; it is not a load. This PR refuses new entries only, as it says.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/cloud-connection: patch` is correct: `Metadata-protocol: none` (no key, value or type an author can write changes; the change is one runtime refusal at one HTTP door), so under ruling A on #25105 and AGENTS.md's level rule ("`none` takes patch; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships patch and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition") the level is patch.
- The `!` in the commit title and the `**BREAKING**` banner are owed: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING by the closed pair's definition, and the banner states what breaks (a cloud-branch caller relying on the lenient answer) and the remedy. This matches the series' landed precedents byte-for-byte in shape: #31388's changeset (`31296-install-local-cloud-bare-name-refused.md`: patch, `fix(cloud-connection)!:`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, BREAKING banner, Before/Now/Unchanged/Remedy) and #31439's (patch, `!`, BREAKING, same marker).
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: the diff exports nothing new. `NAME_HELD_ELSEWHERE_REFUSALS` and `refusesNameHeldElsewhere` are module-private; the two removed functions were module-private and referenced by no other file on main or in the PR tree (`git grep` on both: no hits outside the plugin file). No schema, protocol member, route, query parameter or response key is added. No widening; the arm is right.
- The ADR-0087 disposition line (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) is the right category: no stored row is read differently, no key is added or removed, and the remedy is the rename/uninstall the refusal names. Its sentence agrees with the code as read in ① (nothing for `migrate meta` to rewrite; an earlier entry is read as before). `Check Changeset` on the head is green.
- The PR body carries the same two declaration lines as the changeset, in the same arm.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation: the bare-name harness's `objectql` stub now forwards the engine's `manifests`.** Read against `isWritablePackage` (package-writability.ts 73-83): a holder is read-only when `engine.manifests.has(id)` or when its registry record carries a read-only `scope`; a marketplace manifest carries no `scope`, so without `manifests` the holder this door installed read as writable and step 1f answered `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` first. With `manifests` forwarded, `registerApp` (engine-registration.ts 166) has recorded the holder, so 1f passes and the register meets the namespace gate. The real `objectql` service exposes `get manifests()` (engine.ts 9842, 9948, 9968), so the harness now reads as the service does. The dev's reading (409 without, 200 `hotLoaded: false` on main with) is consistent with the code; the deviation is accepted. Nit noted in ④ about the "read live" wording.
- **Premise measured red on main for both halves** (5 failures on 1ff99441, the three catalog cases and the two namespace cases), as the card asked for the namespace half ("measure first"). Accepted on the report's own reading; not re-run here.
- **`open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`.** No open question is owed. One out-of-scope finding is added by this review (④, should-fix), to be routed to a card by the seat, not to this PR.
- **Gates.** Dev reports 69/69 derived families exit 0, full build 120/120, cloud-connection 75 files / 1000 tests, typecheck 0, dogfood battery 0, eslint 0. Check-runs on 2f6e606d at review time (read three times by `gh api`, last at the write): 40 completed, every one `success` or `skipped` (Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint ESLint, Lint docs & code guards, Lint CI/release/engine gates, Lint repo & tooling gates, Type Check source gates, Type Check consumer gates, Type Check debt ledger, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Test Core 6/8 7/8 8/8, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, Test UI); 6 still `in_progress` when last read: Test Core 1/8 through 5/8 and Type Check workspace. No check had failed. The gate verdicts are the check-runs' own; the seat reads their completion before landing.
- **Governed surface: none** (four paths, none in the register). Draft PR, no assignees; the seat's own claim and this record are its review of record on the narrowing face.

### ④ Design judgment

Tried to break the predicate and the refusal's placement against the cited code:

- **Error subclass or wrapped error.** All three classes assign `this.name` explicitly in their constructors, so a subclass inherits the recognised name unless it overrides it; the cold-boot variants (`door: 'cold-boot'`) are the same classes and are not raised through this door. The chain from `manifestService.register` to `installPackage` (plugin.ts 860-985, engine-registration.ts 150-240, `restoringOnRefusal` registry.ts ~3965-3980) catches nothing and rethrows the original error unwrapped (`throw err`), so no `cause` chain hides the code. A wrapper introduced later would silently drop to the lenient path; that is the same exposure #25366 and #31296 accepted and is the registry's unexported-class choice, not this PR's. No finding.
- **Partial write before the 422.** On the door: steps 1-2e' are reads and refusals; the first write is `this.ledger.write` at step 4, after the catch returns. In the registry: `installPackage` runs the `source` TypeError, namespace gate, co-owned object-name check, security-catalog refusal, default-record-page refusal and bare-name refusal before `registerNamespace` and the package row; `registerApp` wraps the body in `restoringOnRefusal` and writes `manifests.set`, datasource defs and nav contributions only after it returns. So a refused install leaves no registry row, no namespace ownership, no claim, no engine manifest, no ledger entry and no package-store file (the cloud branch writes no file before register; `fetch` at 2356 is a read). The tests assert the registry and ledger halves (`getPackage` undefined / 1.0.0 kept, ledger equal to before). Nothing is left behind. No finding.
- **Upgrade path.** An installed 1.0.0 whose 2.0.0 newly declares a held name: `installPackage` excludes the package's own holdings (`selfId`) and its own namespace (`owner !== manifest.id`), so 2.0.0 is refused only for the OTHER holder; `restoringOnRefusal` leaves 1.0.0 serving whole, and the door's ledger entry for 1.0.0 is untouched. Pinned by both upgrade cases. No finding.
- **Built-in holder.** The package door asks `builtIns: true`; `BUILT_IN_SECURITY_CATALOG_NAMES.position` includes `AUDIENCE_ANCHOR_POSITIONS` (`everyone`, `guest`); the refusal reads `... "everyone" is already held by the platform, as a built-in name ...`, which the test's `expectHeldElsewhereRefusal(res, EVERYONE_POSITION, 'the platform')` matches. No finding.
- **Response body, cloud vs inline.** Both carry `PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED` and the registry's full sentence (both holders, remedy); the prefixes differ (`Package 'id' cannot be installed:` vs `Failed to register imported manifest:`), which #25366 introduced and the card did not ask to change. No `details` on either. Nit at most; not raised.
- **Concurrency with a second install.** The gates and the mutation inside `installPackage` are synchronous within one `registerApp` call, so two awaited installs serialise at the registry and the second meets the first's registration or claim. The door's own await points (fetch, gates) precede the register and write nothing. The PR adds no new window. No finding.
- **Other register failures still on the lenient path that should not be — should-fix, out of scope, route to a card.** The same `installPackage` and `manifest.register` raise other pre-write refusals that no restart heals and that are judged again at every load with the same holder present: `DefaultRecordPageConflictError` (`DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT`, another package's default record page for the same object, registry.ts 4317/7682), `ArtifactObjectNameConflictError` (`DUPLICATE_ARTIFACT_OBJECT_NAME`, 8894), `ObjectOwnershipConflictError` (`OBJECT_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT`, 5175), `MisplacedDefaultPageError` (an authoring error, 4297/7672), and the manifest service's sealed-vocabulary refusals (unresolved picklist references, unbound action targets, plugin.ts 930-976). On the cloud branch each is ledgered and answered `200 hotLoaded: false`, then refused at every rehydrate, exactly the shape #25366, #31296 and this card fix for the three held-name classes. The card's reach is the security-catalog name and the namespace, so this is not a defect of this PR and not a FAIL; the inline branch already answers all of them 422, and the #22695 comment at 3038 still records the lenient path's fate as "a separate decision". The seat should file it as the next sibling on this door (recognise by code for each class, or decide the lenient path's fate once).
- **Nit (test prose only).** The bare-name harness comment says the engine's manifests are "read live" through a getter, but `withInstallerGrants` spreads the stub (`{...engine}`), which evaluates the getter once and copies the Map reference. The engine never reassigns `manifests` (engine.ts 560 only), so the Map is the engine's own and the reading is live in effect. No effect on the test or the contract.
- **Nit (changeset prose).** "A ledger entry an earlier build wrote this way is read as before at boot" is true; "is read and refused at every boot, as before" would say what happens. No effect on the contract.
- **Changeset agreement with the code.** Before/Now/Unchanged and the remedy each match ①: the three classes, the two holders named, nothing registered or written, earlier version kept, `warn` policy unchanged, 1f's 409 unchanged. The module header, import comment, predicate docblock, catch comment and 1f comment in the diff agree with the code they describe.

No must-fix.
